en: The National Mapping and Resource Information Authority officially counts 7,641 islands in the Philippine archipelago.
Mount Apo in Mindanao is the highest mountain in the Philippines, reaching an elevation of 2,954 meters.
Mount Mayon in Albay is famous for its perfect conical shape and has over 50 recorded eruptions.
The Cagayan River in Northern Luzon is the longest river in the Philippines, stretching 505 kilometers.
Laguna de Bay is the largest lake in the Philippines, covering a surface area of over 900 square kilometers.
Palawan is the largest province in the Philippines, consisting of 1,780 islands stretching 425 kilometers long.
The Philippine tarsier is one of the world's smallest primates, measuring only 85 to 160 millimeters in body length.
The Philippines experiences an average of 20 tropical cyclones entering its surrounding waters every year.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River National Park features an 8.2-kilometer underground river that flows directly into the sea.
The Banaue Rice Terraces were carved into the mountains of Ifugao over 2,000 years ago by the Ifugao people.
The Philippines ranks second globally in gold reserves and holds the largest nickel reserves in the world.
The Sierra Madre mountain range is the longest in the Philippines, stretching 540 kilometers along eastern Luzon.
